subject: Elastic seat conversion & SLA buffering for Q4 renewal
messages:
From: Eve Johnson <eve.johnson@brightpath.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos@ops.brightpath.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Elastic seat conversion and SLA buffering for Q4 renewal

Hi Priyom,

We ran into a predictable pattern over the last 6 weeks where our peak inference volume is now holding for longer sustained windows. Our usage team attached a 90-day export (brightpath_90d_usage.csv) — you can see the daily 95th percentile token consumption and the multi-hour sustained windows around our ingestion jobs.

We have a renewal coming up for the Dedicated fleet on Dec 1 and we want to avoid repeated emergency bursts. Our ask: can Redwood propose a conversion path that trades some of our on-demand burst GPUs into a short-term reserved pool (3–6 months) with an SLA buffer so we don’t experience throttling during our nightly inference runs?

Key constraints:
- Keep our 99th percentile latency below 220ms for generation routes.
- Cap increase in monthly committed spend to no more than +18% versus current forecast.
- Provide a plan for a fast rollback to burst if our production regression tests show model quality issues after deployment.

Can you put together a short proposal (capacity counts, pricing delta, and an onboarding timeline) by the end of next week?

Thanks,
Eve
Eve Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightPath

Eve — thanks for the data and clear constraints. Looping in Karthik (capacity planning) and Ben (renewals/pricing).

Immediate next steps from our side:
1) Karthik will run a short utilization sweep against the 90-day export to recommend a minimal reserved seat set that covers sustained windows without oversizing.
2) Ben and I will model the commit delta vs. current burst plan and output a 3- and 6-month financial comparison (pricing + credits).
3) We will include an explicit rollback playbook for your CI gating if model outputs need to revert to on-demand variants.

Can you confirm the expected growth ramp for the next 90 days (conservative %) and any blackout windows where we should not alter routing?

I’ll aim to get a draft proposal back by Mon 11/17.

Best,
Priyom

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 08:38:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity sweep: BrightPath 90d -> candidate reserved set

Team — I ran the utilization sweep on the 90-day file and here are the highlights (brief):
- Sustained windows (multi-hour) occur daily between 02:00–05:30 UTC, median active GPUs required: 28, 95th percentile sustained: 36.
- Short spikes still exist during business hours peaking to ~58 GPUs for minutes.
- Current committed reserved GPUs: 20. Burst pool handles the rest.

Proposal (technical):
- Convert 12 GPUs from burst → temporary reserved pool for a 3-month term (new reserved = 32). That covers the 95th sustained window with ~10% headroom.
- Keep a 24-GPU burst buffer for short, sub-minute spikes. Configure automated routing to fall back to 1) local fallback model variant, 2) then burst pool.
- Enable aggressive KV prefix caching for the nightly ingestion route to reduce token cost without changing SLOs.

Operational notes:
- We need a 48-hour scheduled maintenance window to apply kernel tuning to the reserved instances (low-impact, scheduled off-hours).
- SLA buffer: propose a conditional 12% latency credit if 99th percentile exceeds 220ms for two consecutive days while running the new mix.

I'll hand this to Ben for pricing and Laura for onboarding steps.

Karthik
Capacity Planning Lead
Redwood Inference

To: Eve Johnson <eve.johnson@brightpath.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Elastic seat conversion and SLA buffering for Q4 renewal

Eve — attaching a short analysis (pdf) with pricing scenarios for 3-month and 6-month reserved conversions.

Summary (business):
- 3-month conversion (recommended): move 12 GPUs into reserved at an effective +14% monthly commit (net of burst credits). Estimated monthly cost increase: $19,200.
- 6-month conversion: move 16 GPUs into reserved with a +22% monthly commit, but unit price improves ~9%.
- We can layer in a temporary discounted SLA buffer for the first 30 days to reduce your risk during tuning (one-time credit equal to 10% of the first invoice).

Attachments: 20261117-elastic-seat-analysis.pdf (summary + per-GPU economics)

If this looks good, I’ll prepare an SOW and a short DocuSign request for signature. Priyom — please include the 48-hour maintenance window in the SOW.

Cheers,
Ben
Head of Renewal Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Eve Johnson <eve.johnson@brightpath.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos@ops.brightpath.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Nov 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Elastic seat conversion and SLA buffering for Q4 renewal

Thanks Ben — the 3-month option is closest to our runway, but two asks before we sign:
1) Can you shave 2 GPUs off the reserved conversion and keep them in burst so our peak short spikes are still in a freer pool? (i.e., reserve +10 GPUs vs your +12).
2) We want a 6-week thermal headroom guarantee — essentially a one-time bump window we can call to temporarily add an additional 8 GPUs to reserved capacity for emergency runs, with an agreed pricing floor if called more than twice.

If you can include those two items (revised pricing and a DocuSign link), we can get sign-off from procurement this week.

Eve

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Final: Elastic seat conversion & SLA buffering (SOW v2)

Eve — appreciate the quick turnaround. We updated the plan per your asks and attached SOW-BrightPath-20261121-v2.pdf. Highlights: 
- Reserved conversion: +10 GPUs for an initial 3-month term (reserved total = 30). Burst buffer retained at 28 GPUs.
- Thermal headroom: 6-week callable window where BrightPath can request a temp reservation of +8 GPUs. First two calls: no additional unit uplift; subsequent calls: +12% price floor on called GPUs.
- Maintenance window: 48 hours scheduled week of Nov 29 for kernel tuning; we will coordinate exact UTC windows with your ops calendar.
- SLA buffer: first 30 days we will honor a one-time invoice credit equal to 10% of that invoice if 99th percentile latency exceeds 220ms for two consecutive days. After that, latency credits apply per the SLO addendum.

DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/ABC123BrightPathSOWv2
Drive folder (assets, onboarding runbook): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0BxyzBrightPathOnboarding
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deals/DP-8791

Next steps for BrightPath:
- Procurement: sign via DocuSign (target: Tue 11/23).
- Ops: confirm preferred maintenance window (Laura will follow up).

Internal: Laura — prep onboarding checklist + runbook; Karthik — schedule kernels tuning and pre-deploy tests; Ben — finalize billing cadence and PRs for the 10% credit.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to a smooth rollout.

Best,
